title: Russia Gets a Green Light — But No Flag Yet — for the 2028 Olympics!
summary:
Imagine training your whole life for the Olympics, only to be told you can’t compete because of something your country’s leaders did. That’s what happened to many Russian athletes after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. But now, things are changing! The International Olympic Committee (IOC) just lifted its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee. That means Russian athletes can start joining international sports events again, including the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles.

The IOC suspended Russia back in October 2022 because Russia’s Olympic committee started recognizing sports groups in parts of Ukraine that Russia had taken over. The IOC said that broke the rules. But now Russia says it won’t do that anymore, so the IOC decided to let them back in — for now. IOC President Kirsty Coventry said, “We don’t want to hold athletes accountable for the actions of their government.” She thinks it’s not fair to punish athletes for what politicians do.

But there’s a catch: Russia still can’t show its flag, wear its colors, or play its national anthem at the Games. That decision hasn’t been made yet. At the 2024 Paris Olympics and the 2026 Winter Games, Russian athletes had to compete as “neutrals” — no flag, no anthem. It might be the same in LA.

Ukraine hasn’t said anything yet about this decision. Russian sports minister Mikhail Degtyarev called it “a green light” for Russian athletes to fully return. The IOC says it will keep watching Russia closely and can take more action if needed. So, will we see Russian athletes under their own flag in 2028? Stay tuned!
why_it_matters: It shows that sports and politics often mix, and big decisions about fairness affect athletes who train just as hard as you do for your school competitions.

keywords.explanation: The group of people from many countries that runs the Olympic Games.
Stopped for a period of time, often as a punishment.
Not representing any country; without a flag or national song.
The official song of a country, played at important events.
People who make decisions and laws for a country or region.
An idiom meaning permission or approval to go ahead.

questions.question: Why did the IOC suspend Russia in 2022?
options: Because Russian athletes used banned drugs.
Because Russia's Olympic committee recognized sports groups in occupied parts of Ukraine.
Because Russia refused to host the Olympics.
Because Russian athletes didn't train enough.
questions.correct_answer: Because Russia's Olympic committee recognized sports groups in occupied parts of Ukraine.

questions.question: What did IOC President Kirsty Coventry say about punishing athletes?
options: Athletes should always be punished if their country breaks rules.
It is not fair to hold athletes accountable for their government's actions.
Athletes should never compete in the Olympics again.
Only coaches should be punished, not athletes.
questions.correct_answer: It is not fair to hold athletes accountable for their government's actions.

questions.question: What might Russian athletes still NOT be allowed to do at the 2028 Olympics?
options: Run in the opening ceremony.
Wear their flag, colors, or hear their national anthem.
Speak to reporters.
Stay in the Olympic Village.
questions.correct_answer: Wear their flag, colors, or hear their national anthem.

questions.question: How did Russian athletes compete at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
options: Under a different country's flag.
As neutrals, with no flag or anthem.
They didn't compete at all.
Under the Olympic flag as full team Russia.
questions.correct_answer: As neutrals, with no flag or anthem.

questions.question: What did Russian sports minister Mikhail Degtyarev call the IOC's decision?
options: A yellow card.
A green light.
A red flag.
A false start.

questions.question: What did Russia promise to do so the IOC would lift the suspension?
options: Pay a fine.
Stop recognizing sports groups in occupied Ukrainian land.
Apologize on TV.
Change its national anthem.
questions.correct_answer: Stop recognizing sports groups in occupied Ukrainian land.

background_read: Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, and many countries then stopped doing business or sports with Russia. The International Olympic Committee (IOC) is the group that decides who can join the Games.
Los Angeles is a large city in California, USA, and it will host the Summer Olympics in 2028. This will be the third time LA has held the Games.
The IOC President, Kirsty Coventry, is the first woman and the first person from Africa to lead the Olympic movement.
Article_Structure: WHO: Russian athletes, the International Olympic Committee (IOC), and IOC President Kirsty Coventry.
WHAT: The IOC lifted its suspension of Russia's Olympic committee, so Russian athletes can join international events again, but the final decision about displaying their flag is not yet made.
WHERE: The 2028 Summer Olympics will be in Los Angeles, USA; earlier Games were in Paris.
WHY: Russia says it stopped recognizing sports groups in parts of Ukraine it had taken over, so the IOC allowed them back, but will keep watching closely.

perspectives.description: Many people think it's right to let athletes compete because they are not the ones who started the war. Punishing them for their government's actions seems unfair.
Some feel Russia should not return to the Olympics so soon after invading another country, because the ban sends a strong message against breaking international rules.
The IOC tries to keep politics out of sports, but it also uses rules like the neutral flag to show disapproval while not banning individual athletes.
